sanskrit: etat kāraṇasāmagryaṃ śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ bhavanto hi taponityā brūyur etat samāhitāḥ
english: I wish to hear, in its truth and in the fullness of its causes, this whole matter; for you, ever steadfast in austerity, may set it forth with a composed mind.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas teṣāṃ samastānām ṛṣīṇām ṛṣisattamaḥ ṛṣabho nāma viprarṣiḥ smayann iva tato 'bravīt
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, of all those assembled sages, the foremost of seers, the brahmin-sage named Ṛṣabha, smiling as it were, spoke thus.

sanskrit: purāhaṃ rājaśārdūla tīrthāny anucaran prabho samāsāditavān divyaṃ naranārāyaṇāśramam
english: Long ago, O tiger among kings, O mighty lord, as I wandered among the sacred fords, I came upon the divine hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: yatra sā badarī ramyā hrado vaihāyasas tathā yatra cāśvaśirā rājan vedān paṭhati śāśvatān
english: There stood that lovely jujube tree and the lake Vaihāyasa, and there, O king, Aśvaśiras recites the eternal Vedas.

sanskrit: tasmin sarasi kṛtvāhaṃ vidhivat tarpaṇaṃ purā pitṝṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca tato ''śramam iyāṃ tadā
english: Having duly made my offerings of water to the ancestors and the gods at that lake, I then proceeded to the hermitage.

sanskrit: remāte yatra tau nityaṃ naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī adūrād āśramaṃ kaṃ cid vāsārtham agamaṃ tataḥ
english: There, where the two sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa ever take their delight, I went, not far off, to a certain hermitage to take up my lodging.

sanskrit: tataś cīrājinadharaṃ kṛśam uccam atīva ca adrākṣam ṛṣim āyāntaṃ tanuṃ nāma taponidhim
english: Then I beheld a sage approaching, clad in bark and deerskin, exceedingly lean and tall — a treasury of austerity named Tanu.

sanskrit: anyair narair mahābāho vapuṣāṣṭaguṇānvitam kṛśatā cāpi rājarṣe na dṛṣṭā tādṛśī kva cit
english: O mighty-armed one, in stature he was eightfold beyond other men, yet, O royal sage, such gauntness as his I had never anywhere seen.

sanskrit: śarīram api rājendra tasya kāniṣṭhikāsamam grīvā bāhū tathā pādau keśāś cādbhutadarśanāḥ
english: His body, O lord of kings, was as slender as a little finger; his neck, his arms, his feet, and his hair were a wonder to behold.

sanskrit: śiraḥ kāyānurūpaṃ ca karṇau netre tathaiva ca tasya vāk caiva ceṣṭā ca sāmānye rājasattama
english: His head was in keeping with his frame, and so too his ears and eyes; yet his speech and his bearing, O best of kings, were as those of ordinary men.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvāhaṃ taṃ kṛśaṃ vipraṃ bhītaḥ paramadurmanāḥ pādau tasyābhivādyātha sthitaḥ prāñjalir agrataḥ
english: Seeing that emaciated brahmin, I grew afraid and deeply troubled in heart; and having saluted his feet, I stood before him with hands folded in reverence.

sanskrit: nivedya nāma gotraṃ ca pitaraṃ ca nararṣabha pradiṣṭe cāsane tena śanair aham upāviśam
english: Having announced my name, my lineage, and my father, O bull among men, I slowly took my seat upon the place he indicated.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kathayām āsa kathā dharmārthasaṃhitāḥ ṛṣimadhye mahārāja tatra dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Then, O great king, in the midst of the sages, that best of the upholders of dharma recounted discourses bound up with righteousness and worldly profit.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu kathayaty eva rājā rājīvalocanaḥ upāyāj javanair aśvaiḥ sabalaḥ sāvarodhanaḥ
english: And even as he was speaking, a lotus-eyed king drew near on swift horses, together with his army and his retinue of the inner apartments.

sanskrit: smaran putram araṇye vai naṣṭaṃ paramadurmanāḥ bhūridyumnapitā dhīmān raghuśreṣṭho mahāyaśāḥ
english: Brooding over his son lost in the forest and stricken with the deepest grief — the wise and greatly renowned father of Bhūridyumna, foremost of the Raghus.

sanskrit: iha drakṣyāmi taṃ putraṃ drakṣyāmīheti pārthivaḥ evam āśākṛto rājaṃś caran vanam idaṃ purā
english: "Here I shall behold that son of mine, here I shall see him" — thus, O king, fashioned by hope, that monarch had once ranged through this forest.

sanskrit: durlabhaḥ sa mayā draṣṭuṃ nūnaṃ paramadhārmikaḥ ekaḥ putro mahāraṇye naṣṭa ity asakṛt tadā
english: "Hard indeed is it for me to behold him, that most righteous one; my only son, lost in the great forest" — thus again and again he lamented.

sanskrit: durlabhaḥ sa mayā draṣṭum āśā ca mahatī mama tayā parītagātro 'haṃ mumūrṣur nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "Hard is he for me to behold, yet great is my hope; encompassed in every limb by it, I am surely about to die — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā sa bhagavāṃs tanur munivarottamaḥ avākśirā dhyānaparo muhūrtam iva tasthivān
english: Hearing this, the venerable Tanu, the very best of sages, with head bowed and absorbed in meditation, remained for a moment as if motionless.

sanskrit: tam anudhyāntam ālakṣya rājā paramadurmanāḥ uvāca vākyaṃ dīnātmā mandaṃ mandam ivāsakṛt
english: Marking him sunk in thought, the king, most sorrowful and wretched of spirit, spoke these words, again and again, softly and ever more softly.

sanskrit: durlabhaṃ kiṃ nu viprarṣe āśāyāś caiva kiṃ bhavet bravītu bhagavān etad yadi guhyaṃ na tan mayi
english: "What, O brahmin-sage, is hard to attain, and what may there be of hope? Let the venerable one declare this, if it be no secret kept from me."

sanskrit: maharṣir bhagavāṃs tena pūrvam āsīd vimānitaḥ bāliśāṃ buddhim āsthāya mandabhāgyatayātmanaḥ
english: Now this venerable great sage had once been slighted by that very king, who, in his ill fortune, had taken to a childish frame of mind.

sanskrit: arthayan kalaśaṃ rājan kāñcanaṃ valkalāni ca nirviṇṇaḥ sa tu viprarṣir nirāśaḥ samapadyata
english: For when, O king, the sage had asked of him a golden pitcher and garments of bark, that brahmin-sage, rebuffed, became disheartened and free of all hope.

sanskrit: evam uktvābhivādyātha tam ṛṣiṃ lokapūjitam śrānto nyaṣīdad dharmātmā yathā tvaṃ narasattama
english: Having spoken thus and saluted that sage honoured by the world, the righteous king, wearied, sat down — even as you do now, O best of men.

sanskrit: arghyaṃ tataḥ samānīya pādyaṃ caiva mahān ṛṣiḥ āraṇyakena vidhinā rājñe sarvaṃ nyavedayat
english: Then the great sage, bringing the welcome-offering and water for the feet, presented all to the king according to the rite of the forest-dwellers.

sanskrit: tatas te munayaḥ sarve parivārya nararṣabham upāviśan puraskṛtya saptarṣaya iva dhruvam
english: Thereupon all those sages, encircling that bull among men and setting him before them, took their seats, as the Seven Sages encircle the Pole-star.

sanskrit: apṛcchaṃś caiva te tatra rājānam aparājitam prayojanam idaṃ sarvam āśramasya praveśanam
english: And there they questioned that unvanquished king as to his every purpose and the reason for his entering the hermitage.

sanskrit: rājovāca vīradyumna iti khyāto rājāhaṃ dikṣu viśrutaḥ bhūridyumnaṃ sutaṃ naṣṭam anveṣṭuṃ vanam āgataḥ
english: The king said: I am the king called Vīradyumna, renowned in all quarters; I have come to the forest to seek my lost son, Bhūridyumna.

sanskrit: ekaputraḥ sa viprāgrya bāla eva ca so 'nagha na dṛśyate vane cāsmiṃs tam anveṣṭuṃ carāmy aham
english: He is my only son, O foremost of brahmins, and but a child, O sinless one; nowhere in this forest is he to be seen, and I roam about in search of him.

sanskrit: ṛṣabha uvāca evam ukte tu vacane rājñā munir adhomukhaḥ tūṣṇīm evābhavat tatra na ca pratyuktavān nṛpam
english: Ṛṣabha said: When the king had spoken these words, the sage, his face downcast, fell silent there and made the monarch no reply.

sanskrit: sa hi tena purā vipro rājñā nātyarthamānitaḥ āśākṛśaṃ ca rājendra tapo dīrghaṃ samāsthitaḥ
english: For that brahmin had once been little honoured by this king, and so, O lord of kings, he had undertaken a long austerity, lean and wasted with hope.

sanskrit: pratigraham ahaṃ rājñāṃ na kariṣye kathaṃ cana anyeṣāṃ caiva varṇānām iti kṛtvā dhiyaṃ tadā
english: "Never in any wise shall I accept a gift from kings, nor yet from men of the other castes" — having so resolved in his mind.

sanskrit: āśā hi puruṣaṃ bālaṃ lālāpayati tasthuṣī tām ahaṃ vyapaneṣyāmi iti kṛtvā vyavasthitaḥ
english: "For hope, abiding within, makes a man babble like a child; that hope I will utterly drive away" — thus resolved, he stood firm.

sanskrit: rājovāca āśāyāḥ kiṃ kṛśatvaṃ ca kiṃ ceha bhuvi durlabham bravītu bhagavān etat tvaṃ hi dharmārthadarśivān
english: The king said: What is the leanness of hope, and what is hard to attain here upon earth? Let the venerable one declare this, for you are a seer of dharma and of worldly good.

sanskrit: ṛṣabha uvāca tataḥ saṃsmṛtya tat sarvaṃ smārayiṣyann ivābravīt rājānaṃ bhagavān vipras tataḥ kṛśatanus tanuḥ
english: Ṛṣabha said: Then, calling all of it to mind, the venerable, lean-bodied brahmin Tanu, as if to remind the king, spoke to him thus.

sanskrit: kṛśatve na samaṃ rājann āśāyā vidyate nṛpa tasyā vai durlabhatvāt tu prārthitāḥ pārthivā mayā
english: In leanness, O king, there is nothing to equal hope, O lord of men; and it was because she is so hard to fulfil that I made my entreaties of princes.

sanskrit: rājovāca kṛśākṛśe mayā brahman gṛhīte vacanāt tava durlabhatvaṃ ca tasyaiva vedavākyam iva dvija
english: The king said: Lean and not-lean I have grasped, O brahmin, from your words; and its hard-to-attain nature too, O twice-born, is to me like a saying of the Veda.

sanskrit: saṃśayas tu mahāprājña saṃjāto hṛdaye mama tan me sattama tattvena vaktum arhasi pṛcchataḥ
english: Yet a doubt, O greatly wise one, has arisen in my heart; this, O best of men, you ought to declare to me truly, for I ask it of you.

sanskrit: tvattaḥ kṛśataraṃ kiṃ nu bravītu bhagavān idam yadi guhyaṃ na te vipra loke 'smin kiṃ nu durlabham
english: What, then, is leaner even than you? Let the venerable one declare this, if it be no secret of yours, O brahmin — what in this world is hard to attain?

sanskrit: kṛśatanur uvāca durlabho 'py atha vā nāsti yo 'rthī dhṛtim ivāpnuyāt sudurlabhataras tāta yo 'rthinaṃ nāvamanyate
english: Lean-bodied Tanu said: Hard to find, or rather not to be found, is the petitioner who keeps his composure as if undisturbed; yet harder still to find, my son, is he who does not scorn the one who comes to ask.

sanskrit: saṃśrutya nopakriyate paraṃ śaktyā yathārhataḥ saktā yā sarvabhūteṣu sāśā kṛśatarī mayā
english: The hope that, having heard a promise, is not requited as is fitting and to the utmost of one's power — that hope, clinging to all beings, I deem the leaner one.

sanskrit: ekaputraḥ pitā putre naṣṭe vā proṣite tathā pravṛttiṃ yo na jānāti sāśā kṛśatarī mayā
english: A father of an only son, when that son is lost or gone abroad, who can learn nothing of his fate — his hope I deem the leaner one.

sanskrit: prasave caiva nārīṇāṃ vṛddhānāṃ putrakāritā tathā narendra dhaninām āśā kṛśatarī mayā
english: The hope of women at their delivery, the longing of the aged for a son, and likewise, O lord of men, the hope of the wealthy — these I deem the leaner.

sanskrit: ṛṣabha uvāca etac chrutvā tato rājan sa rājā sāvarodhanaḥ saṃspṛśya pādau śirasā nipapāta dvijarṣabhe
english: Ṛṣabha said: Hearing this, O king, that monarch, together with his retinue of the inner apartments, touched the sage's feet and fell with his head before that bull among the twice-born.

sanskrit: rājovāca prasādaye tvā bhagavan putreṇecchāmi saṃgatim vṛṇīṣva ca varaṃ vipra yam icchasi yathāvidhi
english: The king said: I implore your grace, O venerable one; I long to be reunited with my son. Choose a boon, O brahmin, whatever you desire, in due form.

sanskrit: ṛṣabha uvāca abravīc ca hi taṃ vākyaṃ rājā rājīvalocanaḥ satyam etad yathā vipra tvayoktaṃ nāsty ato mṛṣā
english: Ṛṣabha said: And the lotus-eyed king spoke this word to him: "Even as you have declared, O brahmin, so it is true; there is nothing false herein."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya bhagavāṃs tanur dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ putram asyānayat kṣipraṃ tapasā ca śrutena ca
english: Then the venerable Tanu, foremost of the upholders of dharma, laughing aloud, swiftly brought back his son by the power of austerity and of sacred lore.

sanskrit: taṃ samānāyya putraṃ tu tadopālabhya pārthivam ātmānaṃ darśayām āsa dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Having brought back the son and then admonished the king, that best of the upholders of dharma revealed himself to be Dharma in his own form.

sanskrit: saṃdarśayitvā cātmānaṃ divyam adbhutadarśanam vipāpmā vigatakrodhaś cacāra vanam antikāt
english: And having shown his own divine form, wondrous to behold, free of sin and free of wrath, he departed and ranged through the nearby forest.

sanskrit: etad dṛṣṭaṃ mayā rājaṃs tataś ca vacanaṃ śrutam āśām apanayasvāśu tataḥ kṛśatarīm imām
english: This I myself beheld, O king, and this word I heard; therefore drive swiftly from you this hope, the leaner of the two.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa tatrokto mahārāja ṛṣabheṇa mahātmanā sumitro 'panayat kṣipram āśāṃ kṛśatarīṃ tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, O great king, by the high-souled Ṛṣabha, Sumitrā straightway drove from him then that hope, the leaner one.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvam api kaunteya śrutvā vāṇīm imāṃ mama sthiro bhava yathā rājan himavān acalottamaḥ
english: Even so do you also, O son of Kuntī, having heard this speech of mine, grow steadfast, O king, like Himavān, the noblest of mountains.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi draṣṭā ca śrotā ca kṛcchreṣv arthakṛteṣv iha śrutvā mama mahārāja na saṃtaptum ihārhasi
english: For you are one who has both seen and heard in the hard straits where great deeds were done; having heard me, O great king, you ought not to grieve here any longer.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nāmṛtasyeva paryāptir mamāsti bruvati tvayi tasmāt kathaya bhūyas tvaṃ dharmam eva pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: As of nectar, so of your speaking I can never have my fill; therefore tell me yet more of dharma, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gautamasya ca saṃvādaṃ yamasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount this ancient tale, the dialogue between Gautama and the high-souled Yama.

sanskrit: pāriyātragiriṃ prāpya gautamasyāśramo mahān uvāsa gautamo yatra kālaṃ tad api me śṛṇu
english: Upon Mount Pāriyātra stood the great hermitage of Gautama, where Gautama dwelt for a time; hear of that too from me.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇi so 'tapyad gautamas tapaḥ tam ugratapasaṃ yuktaṃ tapasā bhāvitaṃ munim
english: For sixty thousand years did that Gautama perform his austerity; and to that sage of fierce penance, steadfast and matured by his austerity—

sanskrit: upayāto naravyāghra lokapālo yamas tadā tam apaśyat sutapasam ṛṣiṃ vai gautamaṃ munim
english: —then came, O tiger among men, Yama, the guardian of the worlds; and he beheld that sage Gautama, the muni rich in austerity.

sanskrit: sa taṃ viditvā brahmarṣir yamam āgatam ojasā prāñjaliḥ prayato bhūtvā upasṛptas tapodhanaḥ
english: Knowing him for Yama who had come in his might, that brahmin-sage, that treasury of austerity, with hands folded and self-controlled, drew near to him.

sanskrit: taṃ dharmarājo dṛṣṭvaiva namaskṛtya nararṣabham nyamantrayata dharmeṇa kriyatāṃ kim iti bruvan
english: And the King of Dharma, the moment he beheld that bull among men, made his salutation and addressed him courteously, saying, "What shall be done?"

sanskrit: gautama uvāca mātāpitṛbhyām ānṛṇyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā samavāpnuyāt kathaṃ ca lokān aśnāti puruṣo durlabhāñ śubhān
english: Gautama said: By doing what may a man discharge his debt to mother and father? And how does a man attain to those auspicious worlds so hard to win?

sanskrit: yama uvāca tapaḥśaucavatā nityaṃ satyadharmaratena ca mātāpitror aharahaḥ pūjanaṃ kāryam añjasā
english: Yama said: By one ever endowed with austerity and purity, and devoted to truth and to dharma, honour must be rendered straightway, day after day, to mother and father.

sanskrit: aśvamedhaiś ca yaṣṭavyaṃ bahubhiḥ svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ tena lokān upāśnāti puruṣo 'dbhutadarśanān
english: And sacrifice must be offered with many horse-sacrifices well furnished with their proper gifts; thereby a man attains to worlds wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mitraiḥ prahīyamāṇasya bahvamitrasya kā gatiḥ rājñaḥ saṃkṣīṇakośasya balahīnasya bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For a king forsaken by his friends and beset by many foes, his treasury exhausted and his forces broken, O descendant of Bharata—what recourse remains?

sanskrit: duṣṭāmātyasahāyasya srutamantrasya sarvataḥ rājyāt pracyavamānasya gatim anyām apaśyataḥ
english: —whose ministers and helpers are corrupt, whose counsels have leaked out on every side, who is slipping from his kingdom and sees no other way?

sanskrit: paracakrābhiyātasya durbalasya balīyasā asaṃvihitarāṣṭrasya deśakālāvajānataḥ
english: —assailed by a hostile army, weak before a stronger foe, his realm left unordered, and himself heedless of place and time?

sanskrit: aprāpyaṃ ca bhavet sāntvaṃ bhedo vāpy atipīḍanāt jīvitaṃ cārthahetor vā tatra kiṃ sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: When conciliation cannot be had, nor the sowing of division for want of pressure to apply—and life itself is at stake, or wealth—what then is the righteous course?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca guhyaṃ mā dharmam aprākṣīr atīva bharatarṣabha apṛṣṭo notsahe vaktuṃ dharmam enaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: A secret matter of dharma you have asked of me, O bull of the Bhāratas; unasked, I should not venture to declare this dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dharmo hy aṇīyān vacanād buddheś ca bharatarṣabha śrutvopāsya sadācāraiḥ sādhur bhavati sa kva cit
english: For dharma, O bull of the Bhāratas, is subtler than speech and than thought; only when one has heard it and waited upon it through good conduct does a man somewhere become virtuous.

sanskrit: karmaṇā buddhipūrveṇa bhavaty āḍhyo na vā punaḥ tādṛśo 'yam anupraśnaḥ sa vyavasyas tvayā dhiyā
english: By action governed by intelligence a man becomes wealthy, or else he does not; such is the question you have pressed, and it must be resolved by you with your own discernment.

sanskrit: upāyaṃ dharmabahulaṃ yātrārthaṃ śṛṇu bhārata nāham etādṛśaṃ dharmaṃ bubhūṣe dharmakāraṇāt duḥkhādāna ihāḍhyeṣu syāt tu paścāt kṣamo mataḥ
english: Hear, O descendant of Bharata, of an expedient abounding in dharma, meant for the sustaining of one's course. I would not, for dharma's own sake, wish for such a dharma; yet what brings pain in the taking from the wealthy here is held, in the end, to be allowable.

sanskrit: anugamya gatīnāṃ ca sarvāsām eva niścayam yathā yathā hi puruṣo nityaṃ śāstram avekṣate tathā tathā vijānāti vijñānaṃ cāsya rocate
english: Following out the settled conclusion of all the courses of conduct—the more constantly a man regards the sacred teaching, the more he understands, and the more his understanding gives him delight.

sanskrit: avijñānād ayogaś ca puruṣasyopajāyate avijñānād ayogo hi yogo bhūtikaraḥ punaḥ
english: From want of understanding arises a man's misapplication of means; for from want of understanding comes misapplication, whereas right application, in turn, is the maker of prosperity.

sanskrit: aśaṅkamāno vacanam anasūyur idaṃ śṛṇu rājñaḥ kośakṣayād eva jāyate balasaṃkṣayaḥ
english: Without misgiving and without cavil, hear this my word: it is from the wasting of a king's treasury that the wasting of his forces is born.

sanskrit: kośaṃ saṃjanayed rājā nirjalebhyo yathā jalam kālaṃ prāpyānugṛhṇīyād eṣa dharmo 'tra sāṃpratam
english: Let the king bring a treasury into being, as water is drawn from waterless places; and when the time comes, let him show favour. This is the fitting dharma here and now.

sanskrit: upāyadharmaṃ prāpyainaṃ pūrvair ācaritaṃ janaiḥ anyo dharmaḥ samarthānām āpatsv anyaś ca bhārata
english: Resorting to this dharma of expedients, practised by men of old—one dharma belongs to the powerful, and another, O descendant of Bharata, in times of distress.

sanskrit: prākkośaḥ procyate dharmo buddhir dharmād garīyasī dharmaṃ prāpya nyāyavṛttim abalīyān na vindati
english: A treasury comes first, it is said, then dharma; yet wisdom is weightier than dharma. He who is too weak, even on attaining dharma, does not come by a just course of conduct.

sanskrit: yasmād dhanasyopapattir ekāntena na vidyate tasmād āpady adharmo 'pi śrūyate dharmalakṣaṇaḥ
english: Since wealth is not won by any single, unbending way, therefore in time of distress even what is unrighteous is taught to bear the mark of dharma.

sanskrit: adharmo jāyate yasminn iti vai kavayo viduḥ anantaraḥ kṣatriyasya iti vai vicikitsase
english: "In what does unrighteousness arise?" — this the wise have known; and as to what is nearest to the kṣatriya, on this very point you are in doubt.

sanskrit: yathāsya dharmo na glāyen neyāc chatruvaśaṃ yathā tat kartavyam ihety āhur nātmānam avasādayet
english: That whereby his dharma may not languish, and whereby he may not fall under the power of the foe — that, they say, is to be done here; let him not bring himself to ruin.
